passage: Working Group I of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change has summarized observed changes in annual precipitation across latitudinal bands, comparing the period 1981–2020 with the 1961–1990 baseline. A research team analyzing the IPCC's compiled estimates has argued that, although precipitation has risen across most of the latitudinal bands shown, the change has not been uniform: in particular, the tropical northern band runs against the broader pattern, registering a slight decrease while four of the five bands shown rose. The data shown in the table support this characterization because _______

questionTable.caption: Observed annual precipitation change (% relative to 1961–1990) by latitudinal band, 1981–2020 (IPCC AR6 WG1, Chapter 8)

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the team's claim?

choices.text: four of the five bands rose relative to baseline, while the tropical northern band, at −0.4%, was the only one to record a decrease.
all five of the bands shown registered increases in precipitation relative to baseline, with the tropical northern band's +8.2% change running ahead of the others.
the high northern band registered the largest percentage increase, +8.2% relative to baseline, more than three times the change recorded for any other band shown.

across the five bands shown, the recorded change ran from a decrease of −0.4% in the tropical northern band to an increase of +8.2% in the high northern band, a total spread of about 8.6 percentage points between the two extremes.

explanation: The team's claim has two parts: precipitation rose across most of the bands, and the tropical northern band ran against that pattern with a slight decrease. Only choice A joins both, noting that four of the five bands rose while the tropical northern band, at -0.4 percent, was the lone decrease. Choice C cites only the single largest increase, which cannot show how the bands split. Choice D reports the overall spread of values but not how many bands lie on each side of the baseline. Choice B claims all five bands rose and mistakenly assigns the +8.2 percent figure to the tropical northern band, inverting the very exception the claim depends on.
